explanations: terra: فَلَا تَجْعَلُوا۟ لِلَّهِ أَندَادًا forbids setting up equals for the Creator who provides earth, sky, and fruit; provision does not make the Giver one member of a pair.

terra: The challenge to produce a surah مِن مِّثْلِهِ and call supporting witnesses tests a claimed likeness through collective help, echoing the section’s link between counterpart and added supporter.

luna: The section's root ش ف ع names support by interceding for another; this warning says no soul can avail another and no شَفَاعَةٌ will be accepted on the Day. | terra: On the warned-of day no soul avails another, no شَفَاعَة is accepted, and no help arrives; every form of standing beside someone is removed together.

luna: The section exposes the orphan's lack of support; this covenant commands good treatment of orphans alongside parents, relatives, and the needy. | terra: The covenant pairs worship of God with kindness to parents, kin, orphans, and the needy; the orphan is placed inside an ordered network of obligations.

luna: The section connects support for the orphan with intercession that will fail on the Last Day; this repeated warning likewise denies accepted شَفَاعَةٌ and says no soul will be helped. | terra: No soul can compensate for another and no intercession benefits it, directly staging the judgment-day limit of the section’s “joining as supporter and asker.”
terra: إِلَٰهٌ وَٰحِدٌ declares the worshipped God one and immediately names His mercy, placing divine unity in the stance of dependence and worship.
luna: The section's shafʿ image is one person joining another as a supporter; here those followed disown their followers at judgment and their ties are cut, reversing that imagined support.
luna: The section says hoped-for supporters will not join people at judgment; after 2:166 shows leaders disowning followers, this ayah has followers wish they could return and disown them in turn.

luna: The section says an orphan should be honored and supported; this account of righteousness includes giving one's cherished wealth to orphans. | terra: True righteousness gives cherished wealth to the orphan among named vulnerable recipients; honoring the solitary child becomes a concrete expenditure rather than praise of uniqueness.
terra: Aggression may be answered only “with the like of” what was inflicted; ordinary human retaliation is bounded by a matching counterpart, unlike the unmatched divine punishment in the section.

luna: The section's yatim root marks one left without a matching protector; when asked where to spend, this ayah names orphans among the recipients, reversing abandonment through giving. | terra: Orphans are named among the proper recipients of whatever good wealth is spent, assigning the community a continuing material duty toward them.

luna: The section's orphan is left without someone to join their side; this ayah calls reforming their affairs best and says that mixing lives with them is brotherhood, a direct form of joining. | terra: The command to improve the orphans’ condition culminates in وَإِن تُخَالِطُوهُمْ فَإِخْوَٰنُكُمْ; mixing with them as brothers is the clearest Quranic enactment of not leaving the orphan single.

luna: The section's shafʿ branch is someone joining another as supporter; this Day has no trade, خُلَّةٌ (close friendship), or شَفَاعَةٌ, so even companionship cannot supply help. | terra: Before the day with neither bargaining, friendship, nor شَفَاعَة, giving is urged; present solidarity must occur before those relationships can no longer be used.

luna: The section's root ش ف ع names one who joins another by intercession; this ayah makes intercession conditional, asking who can intercede except by Allah's permission. | terra: مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِى يَشْفَعُ عِندَهُۥٓ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِۦ makes permission the exact boundary: an intercessor can join another’s case only under God’s authority.

terra: The likeness of Jesus before God is explicitly the likeness of Adam; مَثَلَ ... كَمَثَلِ sets two extraordinary created persons as counterparts while their shared Creator remains beyond comparison.
terra: Holding together to God’s rope and refusing division turns former enemies into brothers, describing the act by which separate people become one protected community.
terra: The believers ask to have their sins forgiven and to die مَعَ ٱلْأَبْرَارِ, imagining death as joining the righteous rather than arriving without a company.

luna: The section says creation takes paired form; this ayah describes humanity from one soul and its mate, then the spread of men and women. | terra: Human plurality begins from نَّفْسٍ وَٰحِدَةٍ, receives its mate, and spreads into many men and women; it is the section’s movement from one, to pair, to community in a single creation scene.

luna: The section says the orphan is not honored; this command protects orphans' property and forbids replacing good with bad, specifying material care. | terra: Returning orphans’ property intact protects those who lack a father’s defender and specifies one material form of joining them in support.

luna: The section says the orphan is left unhonored; this ayah makes fear of injustice toward orphans a condition for fair conduct. | terra: The ayah moves from fear of injustice toward orphans to marrying two, three, or four, then restricts the hearer to one if justice is feared; orphan vulnerability, plurality, and the ethical boundary of the single meet in one formulation.

luna: The section's orphan needs someone to stand with them; this ayah requires testing orphans until maturity and delivering their wealth when they are ready. | terra: Testing orphans to maturity and then delivering their property supplies a patient, accountable form of guardianship until they can stand independently.

luna: The section reproaches neglect of the orphan; this inheritance rule directs that an orphan present receive provision and kind words. | terra: When orphans attend an estate division, the ayah commands provision and kind speech for them, bringing those easily excluded into the distribution.

luna: The section's neglected orphan has no advocate; this warning says those who consume orphans' wealth unjustly are consuming fire, marking the boundary around exploitation. | terra: Those who consume orphan property unjustly consume fire into themselves, turning failure to protect the solitary child into an explicitly solitary punishment.

luna: The section reproaches withholding honor from the orphan; this command to show goodness to the orphan places that care among duties owed to God and neighbors. | terra: Doing good to the orphan appears within a long map of near and distant relations, locating the one without a father inside communal neighborliness.

luna: The section ends with a soul joining God's servants; this ayah names the prophets, truthful, martyrs, and righteous as the company of those who obey God and His Messenger, and calls them excellent companions. | terra: Obedience places a person مَعَ ٱلَّذِينَ blessed by God—prophets, truthful, martyrs, and righteous—then calls them excellent companions.

luna: The section's dictionary gloss for ش ف ع describes joining another as نَاصِرًا لَهُ; oppressed men, women, and children here ask for a وليّ and نصير to rescue them, making that support a concrete plea for the vulnerable. | terra: The oppressed men, women, and children ask for a protector and helper, while believers are summoned to fight for them; this enacts the section’s secondary sense of joining another as supporter and petitioner.

luna: The section's root ش ف ع includes joining another as a supporter and asking on their behalf; this ayah says whoever makes a good شَفَاعَةٍ shares in its benefit, giving that social sense directly. | terra: A good or bad شَفَاعَة gives its maker a corresponding share, showing the source root’s social sense as deliberately joining a cause in support rather than merely forming a numerical pair.

luna: The section's orphan needs someone to take their side; this ruling asks for justice to vulnerable orphan girls and forbids withholding what is due them. | terra: The ruling demands justice for orphan women and vulnerable children, extending “honor the orphan” to those whose isolation exposes them to withheld rights.

terra: God will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him; this two-direction divine-human relation is a close nonlexical parallel to “pleased with them and pleased with Him,” and it describes a whole faithful community.
terra: God, His messenger, and the believing worshippers are named as the believers’ allies; this relation explains the attachment through which 5:56 calls them God’s party.

luna: The section's dictionary gloss for entering among عِبَادِي is “among My party”; this ayah names حِزْبَ اللَّهِ as the group whose members prevail. | terra: Taking God, His messenger, and believers as allies identifies one with حِزْبَ ٱللَّهِ; belonging to God’s party is formed through loyal attachment.

luna: The section's root ر ض و is developed as two-sided satisfaction; on the Day truthful people benefit, Allah is رَضِيَ عَنْهُمْ and they are رَضُوا عَنْهُ. | terra: On the day when truthfulness benefits the truthful, رَضِىَ ٱللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا۟ عَنْهُ makes the section’s two-sided satisfaction explicit and associates it with entry into gardens.

luna: The section says the person's hoped-for supporter will not accompany them at judgment; those warned of being gathered have no guardian or شَفِيعٌ besides God. | terra: Those fearing assembly before their Lord are warned that they have no protector or شَفِيع besides Him, sharpening the section’s image of the person without an attached supporter.

luna: The section traces failed worldly care to being left without support; this ayah says the soul held for what it earned has no وَلِيٌّ or شَفِيعٌ besides God. | terra: A soul held for what it earned has neither protector nor شَفِيع and cannot ransom itself, so social and material additions both fail at judgment.

luna: The section's root ش ف ع describes joining another as a supporter, then says people arrive alone; this ayah has them come فُرَادَىٰ and asks where their شُفَعَاءَ are, uniting both claims. | terra: People come to God فُرَٰدَىٰ as first created, and the presumed شُفَعَاء are absent; the ayah itself joins the section’s solitary return to the failure of hoped-for supporters.
terra: God originates the addressed human multitude from نَّفْسٍ وَٰحِدَةٍ, letting plurality retain the trace of a single beginning even without naming the mate here.

luna: The section sets the paired created order against Allah's uniqueness; this ayah asks how He could have a child without a consort (صَاحِبَةٌ) when He created everything. | terra: The Creator of heavens and earth cannot have a child when He has no consort; divine creativity is explicitly separated from creaturely pairing and generation.

luna: The section's claim that created order is paired is made concrete in two sheep and two goats within the eight kinds of cattle. | terra: Sheep and goats are counted as four of ثَمَٰنِيَةَ أَزْوَٰجٍ, making the pair a repeated unit in a larger created total.

luna: The section's paired order continues from sheep and goats to two camels and two cattle; this ayah completes the list begun at 6:143. | terra: Camels and cattle complete the eight pairs begun in 6:143, while the challenge over male and female exposes invented prohibitions imposed on those pairs.

luna: The section says people fail to honor the orphan; this command forbids approaching an orphan's property except in the best way until maturity. | terra: The orphan’s property may be approached only in the best manner until maturity, placing a protective boundary around the child’s vulnerability.

luna: The section says there will be no one to join the condemned as an intercessor; at the unveiling of the promised outcome, they ask هل لنا من شفعاء and find none to speak for them. | terra: Those facing the fulfilled warning ask whether any شُفَعَاء can intercede or whether they can return; their request exposes too late the support they lack.
terra: When God manifests to the mountain He makes it دَكًّا; this concrete crushing supplies the singular prototype for the section’s repeated دَكًّا دَكًّا.
terra: God creates humanity from نَّفْسٍ وَٰحِدَةٍ and makes from it its mate for repose; the single is not left alone but becomes relational.

luna: The section shows care for the orphan as a human duty; this division of spoils assigns a share to orphans, making them recipients of communal provision. | terra: A fixed share of spoils is assigned to orphans, preventing those without a powerful household defender from being omitted from communal wealth.
terra: ثَانِىَ ٱثْنَيْنِ stages two companions under threat, while “God is with us” prevents the vulnerable second from being alone; number becomes loyal accompaniment.
terra: Believing men and women are أَوْلِيَآءُ بَعْضٍ, supporters of one another, so the faithful community is defined by the mutual attachment withheld from the orphan in the section.
terra: Even if the believers are pleased with the excuse-makers, God is not pleased with the defiantly disobedient; human رضى here fails to become the reciprocal رضى of the section.

luna: The section's root ر ض و points to satisfaction between two parties; this ayah says Allah is pleased with the first believers and their followers are pleased with Him, then promises Gardens. | terra: The mutual formula رَّضِىَ ٱللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا۟ عَنْهُ is attached to a named community and prepared gardens, expanding the lone soul’s acceptance into an accepted company.
terra: The command كُونُوا۟ مَعَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ tells the God-conscious to place themselves with a truthful company, a present ethical counterpart to final entry among God’s servants.

luna: The section says the hoped-for intercessor will not stand beside the person by right; here no شَفِيعٌ exists except after His permission. | terra: مَا مِن شَفِيعٍ إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعْدِ إِذْنِهِ makes God’s permission the boundary to all intercessory joining.

luna: The section's shafʿ branch is joining someone as supporter; worshippers call idols their شُفَعَاؤُنَا عِندَ اللَّهِ, exposing the hoped-for support that the section says fails. | terra: The worshippers call other beings “our intercessors with God”; the claim illustrates the imagined attachment that the section says disappears at judgment.
terra: The recompense of an evil is one like it, making equivalence the rule of measured requital and thereby a boundary around the section’s unequalled final punishment.
terra: Those alleging invention are told to bring a surah like it and call whomever they can; the failure of assembled helpers establishes an unmatched object.
terra: The challenge asks for ten fabricated surahs مِثْلِهِ and every available helper, again measuring likeness against the strongest possible human association.
terra: The flood command places مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ in the Ark; paired creatures are preserved together through destruction.
terra: Joseph contrasts scattered many lords with ٱللَّهُ ٱلْوَٰحِدُ ٱلْقَهَّارُ, turning numerical unity into exclusive sovereignty.
terra: Joseph asks تَوَفَّنِى مُسْلِمًا وَأَلْحِقْنِى بِٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ; death is imagined as attachment to the righteous rather than isolated status.

luna: The section says the created world carries pairs; this ayah names two of each kind of fruit, making pairing visible in the earth's produce. | terra: God makes زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ from every fruit, presenting visible created pairs as signs for reflection.

luna: The section's final invitation joins a soul to God's servants; this ayah has the righteous enter Gardens with righteous parents, spouses, and descendants, extending reunion to family. | terra: The righteous enter lasting gardens together with the righteous among parents, spouses, and descendants, making garden-entry the reunion of a person with an accepted community.
luna: The section says no one can stand beside a person against God's judgment; here the weak ask their former leaders whether they can avert any of God's punishment, and the leaders cannot.
luna: The section's image of failed support is echoed when Satan says he cannot answer his followers' calls and they cannot answer his; 14:21 first shows them asking leaders to avert punishment.
terra: All emerge before ٱللَّهِ ٱلْوَٰحِدِ ٱلْقَهَّارِ after earth and heavens are changed, joining the last-day scene to the One before whom each comes.
terra: The criminals are مُقَرَّنِينَ فِى ٱلْأَصْفَادِ—fastened together in fetters; enforced pairing becomes punishment rather than supportive companionship.
terra: “My servants” are defined as a protected group over whom Satan has no authority, except those who follow him; belonging carries a real boundary.
luna: The section turns solitary arrival into belonging among God's servants; in the Garden, God removes rancor and makes its inhabitants brothers facing one another.
terra: أَفَمَن يَخْلُقُ كَمَن لَّا يَخْلُقُ denies likeness between the Creator and non-creators, clarifying why a uniquely made thing cannot share its Maker’s kind of uniqueness.
terra: لَا تَتَّخِذُوٓا۟ إِلَٰهَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ ... إِنَّمَا هُوَ إِلَٰهٌ وَٰحِدٌ makes “two” and “one” the grammar of rejecting any divine counterpart.

luna: The section's pair image takes a social form here: God gives spouses from among people, then children and grandchildren. | terra: God makes spouses from yourselves and from spouses children and grandchildren, showing how a pair opens into the larger human company.

luna: The section's root م ث ل names Iram's counterpart; this ayah uses الْأَمْثَال for likenesses and warns not to set them up for God, preserving His unmatched status. | terra: The prohibition فَلَا تَضْرِبُوا۟ لِلَّهِ ٱلْأَمْثَالَ blocks invented comparisons for God, supporting the section’s move from lexical “counterpart” to divine incomparability.
luna: The section makes each person's final arrival individual; this Day is one when every soul pleads only for itself and is paid in full for what it did.
terra: Abraham, one person, is called an أُمَّةً obedient to God; the ayah collapses the apparent opposition between an individual and a whole faithful community.
terra: If believers retaliate, they must do so only to the like of what they suffered; human punishment has an equal measure even where God’s punishment has no equal agent.

luna: The section's orphan is a person needing another's protection; this command likewise bars approaching orphan property except in the best manner until maturity. | terra: The orphan’s property is protected until maturity and covenants must be fulfilled, making support a binding responsibility rather than sentiment.
terra: God again tells Satan that he has no authority over “My servants,” while divine guardianship suffices for that community.
terra: Humankind and jinn cannot bring بِمِثْلِ هَٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانِ even if they become supporters of one another; unmatched likeness and collective backing meet in one claim.

luna: The section reserves unmatched sovereignty for Allah; this praise says He has no child or partner in dominion and no protector through weakness. | terra: God has neither child, partner in rule, nor protector from weakness; the command to magnify Him follows this threefold denial of any needed counterpart.
terra: God does not share His rule with أَحَدًا, using the source section’s negative indefinite to make the exclusion comprehensive in sovereignty.
terra: The messenger is told to keep himself patiently with those who call on their Lord and not turn his eyes away from them, making steadfast companionship an explicit command.

luna: The section's صَفًّا صَفًّا stages angels in ranks; here all are presented before their Lord in صَفًّا, and the ayah recalls that they return as first created. | terra: People are presented before their Lord صَفًّا and reminded that they came as first created, combining the judgment rank with stripped, original individuality.

luna: The section links the orphan's aloneness with the need for someone to stand by them; the wall protects two orphans' treasure until they mature, by God's mercy. | terra: God preserves a treasure beneath the wall for two orphan boys until maturity because their father was righteous; divine care supplies the protection their absent father cannot.
terra: At the promised time God makes the barrier دَكَّآءَ, another divine leveling that lets the section’s repeated crushing be heard as successive instances of His act.

terra: The messenger is بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ while the revealed God is إِلَٰهٌ وَٰحِدٌ, and worship must associate no أَحَدًا with Him; human likeness, categorical exclusion, and divine unity are assigned to different levels.
terra: هَلْ تَعْلَمُ لَهُۥ سَمِيًّا asks whether any namesake or peer is known for God, restating incomparability without the section’s word مِثْل.
terra: The boastful person loses the wealth and children he claims and comes to God فَرْدًا; earthly additions cannot prevent final singularity.

luna: The section's support branch of ش ف ع is bounded at judgment; this ayah says intercession is unavailable except to one holding a covenant with the Most Merciful. | terra: None possess ٱلشَّفَٰعَة except one who has a covenant with the Merciful, qualifying rather than erasing the section’s image of unavailable support.
terra: Everyone in heavens and earth comes to the Merciful as a servant; 19:94 counts them and 19:95 makes each arrival individual.
terra: God has enumerated them exactly, converting the universal servant-company of 19:93 into distinct counted persons before 19:95 says each comes alone.

luna: The section says each person finally comes without someone joined to their side; فَرْدًا states that everyone comes to God alone. | terra: Every creature comes to God on resurrection فَرْدًا, making the section’s unaccompanied “one” an eschatological condition rather than an abstract number.
terra: Rain brings forth diverse أَزْوَٰجًا of plants; here “pairs” can also carry the sense of kinds, expanding the section’s numerical image into created botanical diversity.
terra: Pharaoh’s magicians are told to assemble their plan and come in a row, making صف a coordinated human formation before the section’s angelic rows.

luna: The section says not everyone can join another as an intercessor; this ayah permits speech and intercession only for one allowed by the Most Merciful. | terra: Intercession benefits only with the Merciful’s permission and approved speech, linking شفاعة to رضى and placing a divine boundary around who may stand beside another.

luna: The section distinguishes the unmatched Creator from paired creation; this ayah says multiple gods in the heavens and earth would bring ruin, marking the boundary of divine oneness. | terra: If heavens and earth contained gods besides God, both would be ruined; cosmic order becomes evidence against divine plurality.

luna: The section's supporter/intercessor can only join by God's leave; this ayah says the angels intercede only for those He approves. | terra: وَلَا يَشْفَعُونَ إِلَّا لِمَنِ ٱرْتَضَىٰ joins the section’s two roots in one rule: intercessors support only someone God has approved.
terra: Zechariah prays, “Do not leave me single,” using فَرْدًا for a human being who seeks the addition of an heir rather than final isolation.
terra: God answers Zechariah, grants him John, and makes his wife fit for him; this ayah supplies the restored family relation requested by the “do not leave me single” of 21:89.
terra: إِنَّ هَٰذِهِۦٓ أُمَّتُكُمْ أُمَّةً وَٰحِدَةً describes a many-person community as one and joins that unity to worship of the one Lord.

luna: The section turns solitude into belonging among God's servants; this promise names عِبَادِيَ الصَّالِحُونَ as a collective who inherit the earth. | terra: God’s righteous servants inherit the earth, giving عِبَادِى a collective promise and a shared destination.
terra: The revived earth grows every beautiful pair or kind, placing paired growth inside the proof of resurrection.
terra: God admits the emigrants and slain into an entrance with which they will be pleased, combining admission with human satisfaction in an afterlife setting.
terra: The injured person first responds with the like of what was inflicted and is then wronged again; the ayah distinguishes measured equivalence from renewed excess.
terra: The repeated Ark instruction carries two of every pair, again making companionship the form by which creaturely kinds survive the flood.
terra: The repeated declaration that the community is أُمَّةً وَٰحِدَةً makes collective belonging and oneness compatible rather than opposed.

luna: The section says true unpaired uniqueness belongs to God; this ayah denies that He took a child or that another god is with Him, against a divided creation. | terra: Had there been multiple gods, each would have taken its creation and risen over the others; the counterfactual makes undivided divine rule incompatible with peers.

luna: At the trumpet, this ayah says kinship ties do not hold and people do not ask one another; it gives the section's arrival alone a concrete severing of family support. | terra: When the trumpet is blown there are no kinship ties and no mutual asking; created relations that normally pair and group people no longer carry them through judgment.
terra: The community is commanded to marry the unmarried among them and the righteous among its male and female servants, turning socially unpaired people into pairs through communal action.
terra: Those unable to marry must remain chaste until God enriches them; this qualifies 24:32 by recognizing that the socially unpaired state can persist under divine provision.
luna: The section opposes created uniqueness to the One who creates; this ayah says Allah has no child or partner in dominion and created all things with measure.
terra: The rejecters are thrown into a narrow place مُقَرَّنِينَ, where being bound together is a punitive parody of the supportive joining developed in the section.

luna: The section says no advocate can match God's judgment; after the worshipped beings deny leading their worshippers in 25:17–18, this ayah says they can neither avert punishment nor help themselves.
terra: The earth produces every noble pair or kind; the repeated formula makes created pairing visible in abundance rather than isolation.
terra: Abraham’s prayer وَأَلْحِقْنِى بِٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ makes being joined to a worthy community a divine gift.

luna: The section says people who failed to support the vulnerable will themselves lack an intercessor; the people in the Fire lament, مَا لَنَا مِن شَافِعِينَ, and the next ayah adds that they have no intimate friend. | terra: The condemned say فَمَا لَنَا مِن شَٰفِعِينَ, naming their lack of anyone able to join their cause.
luna: The section's lone person has no one to join their side; this continuation says there is no حَمِيمٍ (close friend), completing the lament of 26:100's absent intercessors.
terra: Solomon asks God to أَدْخِلْنِى ... فِى عِبَادِكَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ, nearly restaging the section’s singular addressee being admitted among God’s servants.
terra: God promises believers لَنُدْخِلَنَّهُمْ فِى ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ, closely matching the section’s admission of one faithful soul into a collective.
terra: Worldly bonds formed around idols become mutual denial and cursing at resurrection; a false community dissolves when its members most need support.

luna: The section says supposed supporters do not accompany their patrons at the end; this ayah says the partners will not be their شُفَعَاءَ and the patrons will reject them. | terra: Their alleged partners cease to be شُفَعَاء, so supposed association becomes disassociation at the resurrection.

luna: The section connects pairing to mutuality; this ayah says spouses are made for tranquility and that affection and mercy are placed between them. | terra: Mates made from yourselves bring repose, affection, and mercy; the ayah explains pairing as the opposite of abandonment rather than mere arithmetic.
luna: The section's root م ث ل means a peer or counterpart for Iram; here the same root appears in الْمَثَلُ الْأَعْلَىٰ, giving Allah the highest description.
terra: God scatters creatures through the earth and grows every noble pair or kind, linking multiplicity and pairing to His ordering creation.

luna: The section says parents and children cannot keep a person from their own final return; this ayah states a father cannot avail his child nor a child his father on that Day. | terra: No parent can avail a child and no child a parent on the promised day, marking the boundary where even the closest created pair cannot stand in for the other.

luna: The section makes divine judgment the boundary of human support; this ayah says people have no وَلِيٍّ or شَفِيعٍ besides Him. | terra: The denial of any protector or شَفِيع besides God places all effective attachment and advocacy under the unmatched Creator.

luna: The section says intercession cannot supply a match for God's judgment; this ayah says intercession does not benefit except for one He permits. | terra: Intercession does not benefit with God except for one He permits; the ayah marks the controlled exception to judgment-day aloneness.
terra: The command قُومُوا۟ لِلَّهِ مَثْنَىٰ وَفُرَٰدَىٰ places people explicitly “in pairs and singly,” turning the section’s abstract even/odd opposition into a human posture of reflection.
terra: The angels have wings in twos, threes, and fours; a numerical series that includes even and odd is embodied in created heavenly messengers while increase remains God’s act.
terra: Satan summons his party to become companions of the Blaze; this is the opposing destination of a party to the soul’s entry among God’s servants.
terra: Creation from dust and a drop is followed by ثُمَّ جَعَلَكُمْ أَزْوَٰجًا; the movement from small single origin to pairs depends on God’s knowledge.
terra: Shackles reaching the chins picture rejecters immobilized even before the final day, offering a present moral image of the binding later made unsurpassable.

terra: Two messengers are sent and then strengthened with a third, فَعَزَّزْنَا بِثَالِثٍ; addition here is explicitly the addition of support, matching the section’s social definition of joining another.

luna: The section's root ش ف ع includes a person joining another to help them; in the speaker's challenge, the gods' intercession would not avail him or save him. | terra: The believer rejects gods whose شَفَاعَة could not benefit or rescue him if the Merciful intended harm, testing supposed support by its actual power.

luna: The section's claim that created things come in pairs is stated as خَلَقَ الْأَزْوَاجَ كُلَّهَا, extending the pattern to plants, people, and what people do not know. | terra: سُبْحَٰنَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلْأَزْوَٰجَ كُلَّهَا extends pairing across plants, humans, and unknown creatures, while glorification belongs to their Creator.
terra: The people of the Garden recline in shade together with their spouses, showing blessed pairing within the final community.
terra: An oath is sworn by those ranged صَفًّا; it parallels the section’s oath-form opening and its later multiplication of rank after rank.
terra: إِنَّ إِلَٰهَكُمْ لَوَٰحِدٌ makes divine oneness the proposition of an oath passage, resonating with the section’s oath by pair and single.
terra: The wrongdoers are gathered with their counterparts and what they worshipped; judgment supplies a punitive company, reversing the blessed admission among righteous servants.
luna: The section ends with the soul entering among عِبَادِي; after the recompense statement, this ayah exempts God's sincere servants, and the following verses describe their provision and welcome.
luna: The section's soul enters a shared company after being summoned alone; the people of the Garden turn to one another in conversation, showing fellowship after judgment.
terra: The angels say وَإِنَّا لَنَحْنُ ٱلصَّآفُّونَ, identifying the heavenly beings whose ranked presence forms the judgment scene developed in the section.
terra: Solomon asks for a kingdom not fitting anyone after him; its deliberately unrepeatable created distinction remains a granted possession, refining Irem’s boast in being unmatched.
terra: Solomon has other rebellious beings مُقَرَّنِينَ فِى ٱلْأَصْفَادِ; creaturely delegated binding provides a bounded contrast to the final binding whose equal 89:26 denies.
terra: After named torments, the condemned receive other punishments “of the same kind, in pairs”; likeness, multiplicity by pairs, and punishment converge in a single description.
terra: The messenger is told to announce that there is no god but ٱللَّهُ ٱلْوَٰحِدُ ٱلْقَهَّارُ, giving exclusive divine unity a public speaker and addressee.

luna: The section contrasts paired creation with the uniquely One; this ayah rejects a son and closes by naming God الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ. | terra: The ayah denies God a son and closes with ٱلْوَٰحِدُ ٱلْقَهَّارُ, distinguishing His oneness from all creaturely descent and selection.

luna: The section says created things come in pairs; this ayah specifies eight pairs of cattle within the creation and provision of humankind. | terra: One soul, its mate, and eight livestock pairs are placed in one creation account, making singular origin and manifold pairing belong to the one God.
terra: God does not approve disbelief for His servants but approves gratitude for them, specifying what divine pleasure toward the servant does and does not embrace.
terra: The Book is مُتَشَٰبِهًا مَّثَانِىَ—internally resembling and recurrent—so likeness and repetition become a textual form analogous to the section’s doubled units.

luna: The section says people hope for companions who will intercede; this ayah asks whether they have taken intercessors apart from Allah, setting up the answer in 39:44. | terra: The question challenges people for taking شُفَعَاء besides God even when those figures possess and understand nothing, exposing invented companions in one’s cause.

luna: The section's root ش ف ع names advocacy on another's behalf; this answer says all intercession belongs to God, completing 39:43's question. | terra: لِّلَّهِ ٱلشَّفَٰعَةُ جَمِيعًا locates every effective intercession with God, explaining why no added person can rival His judgment.

luna: The section ends with entry among God's servants; this scene has the God-conscious brought to Paradise in groups and welcomed at its opened gates. | terra: Those who feared their Lord are led to the Garden زُمَرًا; the plural companies give a collective counterpart to the single soul’s command to enter.
luna: The section's entry among servants ends in belonging; after the group welcome of 39:73, the Garden's people praise God and say they may settle wherever they wish.

luna: The section pictures a soul admitted among God's servants; the angels pray that God admit the righteous and their righteous parents, spouses, and descendants to Gardens. | terra: The angels ask God to admit the repentant and the righteous among their parents, spouses, and descendants into Eden, explicitly making admission collective across family relations.
terra: At universal emergence God asks who owns sovereignty and answers: ٱلْوَٰحِدِ ٱلْقَهَّارِ; solitary human exposure is set before singular divine rule.

luna: The section's solitary judgment leaves no supporter to join the person; this ayah warns of the approaching Day when no حَمِيمٍ or شَفِيعٍ is obeyed. | terra: On the approaching day wrongdoers have neither devoted friend nor obeyed شَفِيع, combining emotional companionship and formal advocacy in their absence.
terra: Whoever does evil is recompensed only with its like, while righteous believers enter the Garden; matched requital and gracious admission are set side by side.
terra: Collars on necks and chains by which the condemned are dragged render divine restraint as an enacted judgment scene.
terra: After 40:71 places collars and chains on the condemned, this ayah says they are dragged into boiling water and then burned, supplying the destination of those bonds.
terra: “I am only a human like you” is paired with revelation that your God is one, again distinguishing creaturely similitude from the Creator’s unity.

luna: The section's root م ث ل calls Iram peerless; this ayah says there is nothing like God (لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِۦ شَىْءٌ) and immediately names mates and animal pairs, setting created pairing against the Creator's unlikeness. | terra: This ayah holds both sides of the section together: creatures receive أَزْوَٰجًا, while لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِۦ شَىْءٌ denies any counterpart to their Creator.
terra: The recompense of an evil is an evil like it, but pardon and reconciliation are better; equivalence is a ceiling for human response rather than the final word.
luna: The section says creation is paired; this continuation begins God's distribution of daughters or sons as He wills, and 42:50 specifies both sexes together or barrenness.

luna: The section describes created things as paired; this ayah says God may pair sons and daughters or make a person barren, marking a boundary on what pairing means for each family, after 42:49 names one-sex outcomes.

luna: The section's general pair claim appears here in the created pairs and the ships and cattle made for riding. | terra: The One who خَلَقَ ٱلْأَزْوَٰجَ كُلَّهَا also provides ships and cattle for riding; paired creation is integrated into human provision.

luna: The section distinguishes support that truly joins a person from support that fails; this ayah reverses ordinary friendship at judgment, when friends are enemies except the God-conscious. | terra: Close friends become enemies that day except the God-conscious; this boundary prepares the enduring servant-community addressed in 43:68-70.

luna: The section moves from a soul addressed alone to being received among God's servants; God's address يَا عِبَادِ لَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكُمُ الْيَوْمَ welcomes His servants on the Day without fear. | terra: يَٰعِبَادِ directly addresses God’s servants on the last day with freedom from fear and grief; 43:69-70 identifies them and completes their communal entry into the Garden.
terra: This ayah identifies the servants addressed in 43:68 as believers who submitted, giving the group into which the final Garden command of 43:70 admits them.
terra: ٱدْخُلُوا۟ ٱلْجَنَّةَ أَنتُمْ وَأَزْوَٰجُكُمْ commands the servants to enter the Garden with their spouses, combining communal entry and pairing in the closest parallel to 89:29-30.

luna: The section says there is no intercessor to join the condemned; this ayah says those invoked besides Allah do not possess الشَّفَاعَةَ, except a truth-witness. | terra: Those invoked besides God do not possess intercession, apart from the truth-bearing witness who knows; the exception defines legitimate advocacy.

luna: The section says support will not pass from one person to another on the Day; this ayah states that no intimate friend will avail another and none will be helped. | terra: No protective ally avails another at all that day, reversing the section’s social ideal of joining someone as supporter.
terra: Humans may tighten prisoners’ bonds in war, but the same ayah requires later release or ransom; this temporary, regulated bond marks the boundary from God’s incomparable final binding.

terra: The promise that God will not يَتِرَكُمْ your deeds uses the source root و ت ر in its different verbal sense, “deprive or leave deficient”; it lets witr evoke not only being one but being left lacking.
terra: God is pleased with the believers under the tree; this supplies the divine-to-human side of the reciprocal رضى that the section expresses in paired form.
terra: Believers are declared brothers and ordered to reconcile their brothers; it generalizes the “orphans are your brothers” relation into the constitutive bond of the believing community.
terra: Creation as male and female expands into peoples and tribes لِتَعَارَفُوا۟; a pair distinction becomes a network of mutual recognition.
terra: The spread earth produces every beautiful pair or kind, and the next ayah makes this ordered abundance a reminder for the returning servant.

luna: The section states that created order is paired; خَلَقْنَا زَوْجَيْنِ makes the pair form a general feature of creation and says this should prompt remembrance. | terra: وَمِن كُلِّ شَىْءٍ خَلَقْنَا زَوْجَيْنِ states the created order as pairs and makes remembering the Creator the intended inference.

luna: The section's final entry gathers a soul into a community; this ayah says believing descendants are joined to their believing parents without diminishing anyone's deeds. | terra: Believers’ faithful descendants are joined to them in the Garden without reducing anyone’s earned reward; أَلْحَقْنَا بِهِمْ makes blessed attachment itself the gift.

terra: Serving youths are likened to well-protected pearls, again presenting a company of pearl-like figures rather than the lexicon’s single peerless “orphan pearl”; the link is limited to that dictionary illustration.
terra: Let them bring a discourse مِثْلِهِ if truthful: a proposed counterpart becomes the test of a uniqueness claim.

luna: The section's root ش ف ع marks help through intercession; the angels' intercession here cannot avail except after God's permission and approval. | terra: Even many angels’ شَفَاعَة is useless until God permits it for one He wills and approves; multitude alone cannot overcome the solitary judgment described in the section.

luna: The section's pair theme appears in the creation of the male and female pair. | terra: God creates ٱلزَّوْجَيْنِ ٱلذَّكَرَ وَٱلْأُنثَىٰ, defining the pair through male and female and assigning its making to Him.
terra: God is Lord of the two easts and the two wests; the doubled cosmic directions make the created world legible through paired extremities under one Lord.
luna: The section's dictionary branch for ي ت م calls a rare unmatched pearl “an orphan pearl”; this ayah names pearls among the two seas' bounty, though it does not call them rare.
terra: The person who fears standing before his Lord receives two gardens; paired reward answers an individual stance before God.
terra: Each of the two gardens contains two kinds of every fruit, so a paired garden holds repeated fruit-pairs within it.
terra: At resurrection people become three أَزْوَٰجًا, where the word means classes rather than two-member pairs; this different Quranic use shows that a “pair/kind” can name a whole company.
terra: The Garden companions are likened to protected pearls in the plural; this may weakly contrast with the source dictionary’s singular “orphan pearl,” whose rarity rests on having no peer.
terra: No private group of three, five, fewer, or more lacks God’s presence with them; the numbered sequence makes divine accompaniment the answer to apparent human solitude.

luna: The section's gloss connects entering among God's servants with joining His party; this ayah names Satan's party as the defeated opposite, whose members forgot God's remembrance. | terra: Satan takes possession of them and they become حِزْبُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ; it is the opposing community to the divine party into which the faithful soul is admitted.

luna: The section links رضى in two directions and glosses entering among God's servants as entering His party; this ayah says Allah is pleased with believers and they with Him, and calls them حِزْبَ اللَّهِ. | terra: رَضِىَ ٱللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا۟ عَنْهُ states the two-way pleasure developed in the section, then names those people حِزْبُ ٱللَّهِ, matching its gloss of entering God’s servants as entering His party.

luna: The section connects neglect of the orphan to moral failure; this distribution names orphans among the recipients and prevents wealth from circulating only among the rich. | terra: Orphans receive a share of restored property so wealth does not circulate only among the rich, connecting their inclusion to the shape of the whole economy.
terra: Those who fight in God’s way صَفًّا are likened to a compact structure; a row becomes the visible form of persons joined so none stands unsupported.

luna: The section repeats the crushing of earth as دَكًّا دَكًّا; this Day's earth and mountains are crushed in دَكَّةً وَاحِدَةً, using the same root for one final blow. | terra: Earth and mountains are crushed دَكَّةً وَٰحِدَةً, a “single crushing” that illuminates by contrast the section’s paired repetition דَكًّا دَكًّا.

luna: The section says no one can bind as God binds; the command to seize and shackle the condemned begins that judgment scene, continued by fire and a long chain in 69:31–32. | terra: The command “seize him and shackle him” begins a divine binding sequence; 69:31-32 names the fire and the immense chain that complete the unmatched punishment scene.

luna: The section pairs unmatched punishment with binding; this command sends the seized person into Hellfire, between the seizure in 69:30 and the chain in 69:32. | terra: This ayah places the seized person in Hell between the shackling command of 69:30 and chaining of 69:32, identifying the setting and purpose of the bonds.

luna: The section names God's unmatched binding; this scene specifies a chain seventy cubits long, completing 69:30–31's seizure and punishment. | terra: فِى سِلْسِلَةٍ ... فَٱسْلُكُوهُ gives the binding a seventy-cubit chain, concretizing the divine وثاق whose like the section denies to anyone else.

terra: Failure to urge feeding the needy precedes the declaration in 69:35 that the condemned person has no devoted friend, giving textual support to the section’s moral link between withheld care and later aloneness.
terra: فَلَيْسَ لَهُ ٱلْيَوْمَ هَٰهُنَا حَمِيمٌ makes the one who did not promote feeding in 69:34 friendless on that day.

luna: The section says no supporter will accompany the person at judgment; this ayah says no close friend asks after a close friend, and the next ayat imagine relatives offered as ransom. | terra: No close friend asks about a close friend, so intimate companionship ceases to function in the judgment scene.

luna: The section depicts the singular arrival; this Day instead displays friends to one another while each is too occupied to ask after them, as 70:10–14 explains. | terra: Though former intimates are made visible to one another, the guilty person would ransom himself with his children; visibility without solidarity completes 70:10’s failed companionship.
luna: The section says the solitary person cannot count on a supporter; this continuation names brother as a ransom, with 70:10's unasked friend and 70:13–14 widening the loss.
luna: The section's final aloneness is echoed by the wish to ransom one's clan; 70:10–12 establish failed friendship and family, and 70:14 makes the wish universal.
luna: The section says no one can stand in for the person; this ayah imagines giving everything on earth to save oneself, completing the ransom list in 70:10–13.
terra: The jinn exalt their Lord’s majesty because He has taken neither consort nor child, again placing generative pairing outside divine uniqueness.
terra: The messenger says he calls on his Lord and associates with Him no أَحَدًا, using categorical negation to enact exclusive worship.
terra: The messenger says no one can protect him from God and he can find no refuge besides Him, a direct statement of how every merely created supporter fails before divine judgment.
terra: أَنكَالًا وَجَحِيمًا promises shackles and a blaze with God, supplying another direct scene of His eschatological binding.
terra: Choking food and painful punishment follow the shackles and Blaze of 73:12, completing that ayah’s divine restraint scene with what the bonds lead to.

terra: God tells the messenger to leave Him with the person He created وَحِيدًا, after which the passage lists the wealth and sons added to that original solitude; created singleness, additions, and punishment form one arc.

luna: The section says the hoped-for support of an intercessor will not remain at judgment; شَفَاعَةُ الشَّافِعِينَ explicitly does not benefit the damned. | terra: فَمَا تَنفَعُهُمْ شَفَٰعَةُ ٱلشَّٰفِعِينَ explicitly makes even existing intercessors’ advocacy useless to the condemned, as the section states.

luna: The section's pair theme appears again as God makes from the drop male and female. | terra: From the fashioned human drop God makes ٱلزَّوْجَيْنِ ٱلذَّكَرَ وَٱلْأُنثَىٰ, so paired life arises from a single small origin.
terra: Chains, iron collars, and a blaze are prepared for rejecters, detailing the forms taken by divine restraint.

luna: The section makes support for the orphan the human form of joining another; these righteous people feed the orphan, poor, and captive despite loving the food. | terra: The righteous feed an orphan, alongside the needy and captive, despite loving the food; practical care attaches the unprotected person to a giving community.

luna: The section says creation is arranged in pairs; خَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا applies that form directly to human beings. | terra: وَخَلَقْنَٰكُمْ أَزْوَٰجًا states human pairing as a direct act of creation.

luna: The section pictures angels standing ṣaffan ṣaffa; this Day has the Spirit and angels standing in صَفًّا, adding their silence until the Most Merciful permits speech. | terra: The Spirit and angels stand صَفًّا and speak only by the Merciful’s permission; angelic rank and restricted advocacy meet in one last-day scene.

luna: As the section moves from the solitary soul to its final company, this Day-of-Resurrection scene has a person flee from his brother; the next ayat extend the flight to parents and family. | terra: A person flees from his brother, beginning a family-by-family dissolution of companionship at resurrection that continues through 80:37.

luna: The section's account of a person without an earthly supporter meets this scene of fleeing from one's mother and father; 80:34 begins the list and 80:36 continues it. | terra: Mother and father are the next relations fled from, showing that the judgment-day singleton is detached even from the pair that produced him.

luna: The section's solitary arrival is echoed by a person fleeing wife and children; 80:34–35 begin the family list, and 80:37 says each is occupied with his own concern. | terra: A spouse and children are also fled from, undoing the household pair and its descendants in the same scene.

luna: The section says everyone comes alone; this ayah concludes the fleeing-family scene by saying each person has enough concern of his own, completing 80:34–36. | terra: Each person has a concern sufficient for him, explaining the solitary self-absorption behind the flights listed in 80:34-36.

luna: The section says each person comes فَرْدًا, alone; this resurrection scene says souls are paired (زُوِّجَتْ). The pairing's referent is uncertain, so it offers a specific possible reversal of solitary arrival. | terra: At the upheaval of the last day, the souls are paired, وَإِذَا ٱلنُّفُوسُ زُوِّجَتْ; this directly complements the section’s single soul being joined to a company at the end.

luna: The section's solitary return has a close parallel in a Day when no soul can do anything for another and all command belongs to God. | terra: No soul possesses anything for another soul and command belongs wholly to God; repeated نَفْسٌ لِّنَفْسٍ pairs the words while denying effective mutual aid.
terra: لَتَرْكَبُنَّ طَبَقًا عَن طَبَقٍ describes passage from stage to stage; succession, rather than a static count, makes one comparable unit follow another.

luna: The section says no one inflicts punishment like God's; this ayah calls His punishment for the arrogant الْعَذَابَ الْأَكْبَرَ, a specific superlative parallel. | terra: God subjects the one who turns away to ٱلْعَذَابَ ٱلْأَكْبَرَ, presenting His punishment as the greatest and thus directly supporting the section’s claim that no punisher matches Him.

luna: The section says a solitary orphan needs support; this account of the steep path names feeding an orphan who is a relative as a concrete act of care. | terra: Feeding يَتِيمًا ذَا مَقْرَبَةٍ on a day of hunger makes kinship with an orphan a demanding path of moral ascent.
terra: The oath by the creation of male and female parallels the oath by even and odd, giving the section’s numerical pair a bodily created form.
terra: The self-purifying giver who seeks only his Lord’s face “will surely be pleased,” linking human رضى to prior selfless giving.
terra: The Lord’s future gift will make the addressee pleased, presenting divine giving as the cause of the servant’s رضى even though reciprocity is not stated here.

luna: The section calls the orphan one left without a counterpart and needing someone to stand with them; this ayah recalls God finding the Prophet an orphan and sheltering him. | terra: أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيمًا فَـَٔاوَىٰ answers orphaned singularity with God-given shelter, providing the positive model for standing beside the orphan.

luna: The section condemns failure to honor the orphan; this command فَأَمَّا الْيَتِيمَ فَلَا تَقْهَرْ turns that neglect into a prohibition on overpowering the vulnerable child. | terra: فَأَمَّا ٱلْيَتِيمَ فَلَا تَقْهَرْ turns remembered shelter into a direct prohibition against overpowering the unprotected orphan.

luna: The section hears reciprocal satisfaction in its paired forms; this ayah uses the same two-way رضو wording and places it with Gardens beneath which rivers flow. | terra: God is pleased with them and they with Him, and gardens follow; this makes the paired رضى relation the condition of the same communal garden-ending heard in 89:28-30.

luna: The section pairs neglect of the orphan with failure to urge food for the poor; this ayah frames repelling the orphan and not urging the poor's food as the conduct of one who denies Judgment, while 107:2–3 detail the acts.

luna: The section says people fail to honor the orphan; this ayah describes the denier of judgment as يَدُعُّ الْيَتِيمَ, repelling the orphan, making the failure visible. | terra: فَذَٰلِكَ ٱلَّذِى يَدُعُّ ٱلْيَتِيمَ is the exact moral reversal of honoring and joining the orphan: the denier violently drives the solitary child away.

luna: The section's adjacent 89:18 condemns not urging food for the poor alongside neglecting the orphan; this ayah condemns failure to urge that feeding, completing 107:2's paired neglect. | terra: The one who drives away the orphan also fails to urge feeding the poor, showing neglect as a paired social pattern rather than an isolated offense.

luna: The section's root ء ح د is glossed in 89:25–26 as “anyone” under negation; here أَحَدٌ positively names Allah as One, moving from no human match to God's absolute uniqueness. | terra: ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ gives true oneness to God, directly grounding the section’s distinction between a remarkable created singleton and the One without ontological peer.
terra: ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ names the One on whom all depend, explaining why His oneness is not the loneliness or need of a created singleton.
terra: He neither begets nor is begotten, excluding the generational relations by which created beings form pairs and lines of descent; it completes 112:1 and 112:4’s incomparable oneness.

luna: The section says Iram's unmatched status is only created uniqueness and reserves true peerlessness for God; كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ says no equal belongs to Him. | terra: وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ denies every equivalent to God, supplying the precise boundary behind the section’s language of an unmatched counterpart.
